executiveSummary: Castricum's generated 2025 identity, population, neighbourhood, place and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the focused deterministic gate passes all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Release remains correction-required. The coastal preset becomes critical at T+6 and reports 25,140 affected people-equivalent at T+24, but no selected North Sea boundary condition, dune-failure/overtopping state, connected inundation footprint, arrival or recession supports that precision. A controlled T+24 wildfire placed exactly at the Duingebied neighbourhood centre ranks its source only 11th of 19, behind Limmen Oost 5.218 km away; seven unrelated hazards reuse the same complete neighbourhood order. Official HHNK, PWN and VRNHN evidence instead distinguishes the managed dune defence, east/northeast polder and sewer mechanisms, Castricum's dune drinking-water process, wind-driven vegetation fire, limited access and interregional response. De Woude's ferry dependency and specific emergency-service coordination are absent from the logical graph. All exact service values, affected counts and recovery curves are deterministic exercise outputs, not observations, warnings, forecasts, outage reports, evacuation decisions or operator commitments. Public CBS/PDOK, NWB, ProRail, HHNK, LIWO, Waterinfo, KNMI, RIVM, RDI and provider-territory data can improve context, while unavailable or security-sensitive topology, capacity, backup, crews and restoration must remain Unknown or transparently synthetic.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, safety-region and settlement inputs
supports: GM0383 identity, province Noord-Holland, generalized boundary, 36,618 residents, density 738/km², 26.8% aged 65+ and 5,656 one-person households
Nineteen neighbourhoods, four BAG woonplaatsen and CBS rounding/suppression/null semantics; published neighbourhood population sums to 36,605, thirteen below the municipal total
CBS OData and PDOK CBS OGC APIs are annual CC BY 4.0; BAG woonplaatsen are Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0 with source date 2025-07-01 and yields ten local settlement labels
Generalized polygons are suitable for overview selection and municipal aggregation, not local hydraulic, dune, road, building or asset intersection

evidenceSources.title: E02 — NWB, rail, transit and conditional ferry-access context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; transport snapshot 2026-09-02; municipal ferry page 2026
supports: NWB/ProRail are machine-readable CC0 context; NWB is monthly and the current bundle resolves A9, N203, N246 and N512 cross-boundary corridors, the internal N513 geometry and Castricum station
The static OVapi/NDOV-derived snapshot contains 49 stop areas in the generalized boundary and is best-effort without an SLA; static geometry and schedules are not incident-time operation or capacity

The municipality operates Akersloot and De Woude ferries, publishes seasonal/daily operating windows and maintenance pauses, and offers SMS notifications for outages: https://www.castricum.nl/aanvragen-en-regelen/pont-akersloot-en-de-woude

The 13 February 2024 municipal decision list records a dedicated cooperation note for emergency services on island De Woude: https://www.castricum.nl/fileadmin/Castricum/documenten-per-onderwerp/besluitenlijsten-college/2024/Besluitenlijst-BenW-Castricum-13-februari-2024.pdf
No stable machine-readable municipal ferry-status API or reuse licence was found; schedule pages are official context and live state must remain Unknown unless confirmed

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regional risk, crisis-response and current Castricum dune-fire evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2022–2023; policy plan 2024–2027; local exercise June 2026
supports: VRNHN's risk profile distinguishes North Sea/Wadden/IJsselmeer-Markermeer flooding, polder-dike failure and shorter cluster-rain effects; it also describes long electricity loss, gas-transport incidents, care disruption, cyber and wildfire cascades: https://www.vrnhn.nl/sites/vrnhn/files/2022-03/Regionaal%20risicoprofiel%202022%20-%202023%20VRNHN.pdf

The profile states coastal nature areas are susceptible to large forest/dune fires, drought increases risk, and fire control and evacuation around coastal settlements and recreation can be difficult and time-consuming

On 16 and 23 June 2026 VRNHN, neighbouring regions and PWN exercised a fire near Castricum's glider airfield; wind, dry vegetation, paths, vegetation type, drones, firefighting water, communication and possible campsite evacuation were decision-relevant
The exercise found incompatible operational map scales and incomplete interoperability between digital systems; it is an exercise, not observed fire behaviour or a resource guarantee

VRNHN says it lacks the availability insight needed to guarantee deployment and cannot handle multiple large wildfires simultaneously: https://www.vrnhn.nl/actueel/2025-11-25-reactie-op-inspectierapport-grenzen-bereikt-van-de-inspectie-justitie-en
Official plans and news pages provide scenario/governance context; no open live-capacity API, fixed refresh cadence or explicit document reuse licence was established

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Local water responsibilities, climate vulnerability, emergency roles and coastal occupancy context
supports: The municipality advises households to prepare for the first three days and defines its roles in reception, family information, crisis communication, aftercare and safe public space; this is guidance and governance, not proof of household stock or an automatic action

The municipality assigns household/rain wastewater and public-space groundwater duties to itself, surface water/dikes to HHNK, clean drinking water and forest/dune management to PWN, and infrastructure/nature/environment to the province: https://www.castricum.nl/aanvragen-en-regelen/wateroverlast/

The 2023 environmental vision distinguishes intense rain/water nuisance, heat, drought, robust water storage/infiltration and freshwater availability and recognizes Castricum station and mobility: https://www.castricum.nl/fileadmin/BUCH/visie-en-beleid/Castricum/bouwen-en-wonen/Omgevingsvisie-gemeente-Castricum-22-november-2023.pdf

The municipality identifies seasonal beach rescue/EHBO, a 24/7 alarm team and restrictions on ordinary vehicle access: https://www.castricum.nl/over-de-gemeente/recreatie-toerisme-en-strand/strandregels-en-veiligheid
These web pages and PDFs expose no stable API, open-data licence, live occupancy, shelter capacity, ferry status, emergency stocks, crews or completed action state

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Castricum coastal-defence, polder/drainage and machine-readable water-system context
evidenceSources.edition: Legger Wateren vastgesteld 2025; HWH snapshot 2026-09-02; HHNK stress study 2019
supports: HHNK's 2025 ArcGIS service exposes pumps, sluices, weirs and other structures in RD New through WMS/WFS/REST queries and supports JSON, GeoJSON and PBF; service metadata states edition 2025 but no fixed refresh cadence or standard reuse-licence identifier

Companion primary/regional defence and surface-water/retention services are available from https://kaarten.hhnk.nl/arcgis/rest/services; the drought-allocation peilgebied layer is queryable at https://kaarten.hhnk.nl/arcgis/rest/services/ws/WS_Waterverdeling_bij_droogte_Peilgebieden/MapServer, but its licence and cadence are unstated

The generated HWH intersection contains 174 context objects: 50 surface-water pumps, four sewer pumps, three sluices and 117 weirs; HWH OGC APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0 national aggregations with contributor-dependent completeness: https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2

Named context includes Groot-Limmerpolder Zuid, Schulpvaart, Binnengeesterpolder, Hempolder Akersloot, Gemaal 1879, Westwouderpolder and Zeeweg pumps plus sewer pumps for Castricum, Limmen, Akersloot and De Woude; published numeric capacity fields lack a safe unit contract in the app and must not drive flow

HHNK's study says water-system inundation likelihood is high in meadows east/northeast of Castricum while built-up Castricum more often experiences ponding from paving and limited sewer discharge, with potentially high building/infrastructure damage: https://www.hhnk.nl/_flysystem/media/monitoringsrapportage_2019_0.pdf

HHNK identifies dunes as a natural defence and models future weak spots; Castricum notches are managed only where the dune is much wider than the first row. These policy/future layers do not prove a present breach: https://www.hhnk.nl/beheerstrategie

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Castricum dune infiltration, drinking-water reserve and local water-retention context
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator pages; De Zanderij update December 2025–2026
supports: PWN identifies De Kwal as the intake of the Castricum infiltration area: IJsselmeer water is pretreated at Andijk, conveyed to the dunes, filtered for approximately three weeks, pumped through wells and sent for final treatment

PWN documents a 52 km Andijk pipeline, Castricum/Heemskerk infiltration areas and a large stored coastal water reserve usable during calamities: https://www.pwn.nl/drinkwater/water-zuiveren-in-de-natuur
De Zanderij between Castricum and the dunes stores heavy rainfall to reduce local nuisance and helps protect the dune freshwater reserve: https://www.pwn.nl/omgeving/de-zanderij

The operator pages are process/context evidence and expose no documented open machine API, licence, fixed cadence, complete pipe topology, pressure, quality, reserve volume, pump state, backup or restoration suitable for causal ingestion

evidenceSources.title: E07 — LIWO scenario catalogue and Waterinfo observations
supports: LIWO provides professional flood/water-nuisance map layers and explicitly requires specialist water-manager interpretation; the latest listed release is 2025.1.6 dated 30 October 2025

The public WFS at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities exposes scenario/breach, depth, arrival, duration, warning and evacuation-fraction products; a layer/event, version, units, provenance, terms and expert approval must be pinned before it affects simulation
No fixed LIWO release cadence or reusable licence suitable for redistribution was established; absence of a selected layer is Unknown, never zero inundation or safety

Waterinfo provides current point observations for levels, discharge, waves, wind, salinity and temperature; LMW records are generally produced every ten minutes and CC0 unless a component states otherwise: https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/waterdata
Waterinfo is non-mission-critical public context and point observations are not a hydraulic footprint, breach, warning, forecast or scenario clock

evidenceSources.publisher: KNMI / NIPV / RIVM / RDI / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Rijksoverheid
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Integration-ready weather, fire, care, telecom, provider and first-72-hour context
supports: KNMI ten-minute observations are continually updated NetCDF under CC BY 4.0 and may be delayed/corrected; five-minute radar WMS is also CC BY 4.0. These can anchor observed event context, not an arbitrary future scenario

NIPV's professional Risico Index Natuurbranden uses 17 parameters on a one-kilometre grid; no public bulk API, reuse licence or fixed cadence was found: https://nipv.nl/informatievoorziening/voorzieningen/risico-index-natuurbranden/

RIVM's 2026 v1.1 acute-care questionnaire is national CC0 context; no listed acute hospital is inside GM0383 and nearest listed locations are Rode Kruis Ziekenhuis 8.71 km and Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep Alkmaar 8.85 km straight-line: https://datacatalogus.rivm.nl/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.21945/8E767B2D-9CED-4A85-A95D-3AC1A608C663

RDI's public WFS snapshot has 60 antenna records in the generalized boundary but states no reuse licence or cadence; records are locations/functions, not coverage, backhaul, power/backup, congestion or availability: https://antenneregister.nl/mapserver/wfs/

Mijn Aansluiting's live Public Domain WMS/WFS resolves the centre to Liander electricity (updated 2026-03-24), Stedin gas (2025-12-17), PWN water (2025-09-07), no drainage record and Ziggo media; it is provider-supplied responsibility context, not full-boundary coverage or topology: https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/wfs?service=wfs&version=2.0.0&request=getcapabilities

Denk Vooruit describes 72-hour power-loss cascades into telecom, heating and water pressure and recommends household preparation; it is preparedness guidance, not a recovery guarantee: https://www.denkvooruit.nl/risicos/risicos-in-nederland/geen-stroom

identity.summary: The generated code, name, province and safety-region assignment agree with official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, municipality bundle code and bundle name all equal GM0383 / Castricum.
The municipal centre [4.690063454276417, 52.553855742781344] lies inside the generalized 2025 polygon.
The official safety-region layer assigns GM0383 uniquely to Veiligheidsregio Noord-Holland-Noord.

geography.summary: The overview boundary is coherent but cannot resolve Castricum's sea-dune, infiltration, binnenduinrand, polder, canal, lake or island mechanisms.
notes: The municipality spans the North Sea coast and dune reserve through built-up Castricum/Bakkum to Limmen, Akersloot, De Woude and low water-managed land; one centre-distance factor cannot represent this geography.
Official evidence distinguishes the managed coastal dune defence, Castricum infiltration area, De Zanderij retention, east/northeast polder inundation, built-up sewer ponding and island/ferry access.
Use full-resolution boundaries and explicitly selected hydraulic/fire/access footprints; generalized BAG/CBS boundary intersection remains an overview caveat.

demography.summary: Municipal totals match CBS 2025 and neighbourhood population reconciles within small-area publication rounding.
notes: Official/generated population is 36,618, density 738/km², age 65+ is 26.8%, one-person households number 5,656, and published neighbourhood age-65+ count totals 9,805.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 36,605, thirteen below the municipal total (-0.036%); the deterministic allocator reconciles exactly to 36,618.

Resident aggregates do not identify people present at beach, campsites, schools, station, care settings or seasonal recreation, individual vulnerability, evacuation need or household emergency stocks.

regionalDetail.summary: All nineteen neighbourhood rows load, but missing fields remain Unknown and no row is a hazard footprint or live demand surface.
notes: Largest published neighbourhoods are Akersloot West 3,470, Molendijk 3,360, Limmen West 3,080, Oranjebuurt 2,995 and Albert's Hoeve 2,800.
District-heating and public-charging fields have 0/19 usable values; cars per household has 17/19 and three benefit counts have 18/19. Missing values correctly remain null, never zero.
CBS doctor/supermarket distance and age/household aggregates are planning context, not incident-time care, food, fuel, transport or self-reliance.

settlements.summary: BAG places and BRT settlements resolve without label-centre leakage, including De Woude and Castricum aan Zee.
notes: BAG woonplaatsen are Akersloot, Castricum, de Woude and Limmen; BRT additionally identifies ten woonkern/deelkern/gehucht/buurtschap labels including Bakkum, Castricum aan Zee, De Woude and Stierop.
BAG place centres lie within the generalized municipality boundary and no label-point substitution was detected.
Settlement labels and source population metadata are descriptive; they do not establish island access, beach/campsite occupancy, shelter capacity or a causal exposure footprint.

transport.summary: The inter-municipal NWB graph is coherent, but it omits Castricum's decisive local N513/beach, island-ferry and conditional public-transport access from first-72-hour mobility.
notes: The graph has six source-backed cross-boundary links: A9 to Heiloo/Uitgeest, N203 to Heiloo/Uitgeest, N246 to Alkmaar and N512 to Bergen, totaling 1,060 abstract nominal units.

N513 appears in the road geometry but, as an internal coastal/duin access corridor, does not become a logical route. The graph has no Akersloot or De Woude ferry edge and no isolated-island access state.

The official ferry page includes recurring closure windows and SMS outage notices, and the municipality records specific emergency-service cooperation for De Woude; neither is represented in scenario time.

Castricum station and 49 GTFS stop areas are static context. No NDW situations intersected the current cached boundary snapshot; that is Unknown coverage/state, not clear/open roads or functioning rail/ferries.

emergencyContext.summary: Official municipal and VRNHN roles exist, but current warnings, decisions, vulnerable occupancy, resource confirmation and continuity actions are absent.
notes: The municipality's reception, information, communication and aftercare roles and VRNHN's multi-agency structures are situation-driven; they do not validate automatic evacuation, shelter, resource arrival or status changes.

No RIVM-listed acute hospital lies inside GM0383; straight-line distances of 8.71 km to Rode Kruis Ziekenhuis and 8.85 km to Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep Alkmaar do not establish ambulance travel, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion or generator endurance.

Twenty-eight DUO education locations, eight government-register points and 60 RDI antenna records are public context only, not verified shelters, distribution hubs, command posts, care capacity or communication availability.
VRNHN's 2026 exercise identifies real interregional, map, radio, water and campsite-evacuation considerations while its 2025 response expressly rejects guaranteed resource inference.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets produce complete finite output at every required checkpoint and service, with evidential defects recorded separately.
notes: The focused matrix executed severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Status sequences at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 are storm operational/operational/strained/degraded/recovering/operational; pluvial operational/strained/strained/strained/recovering/operational; river all operational; coastal operational/critical/critical/critical/critical/recovering; heat operational/operational/strained/strained/recovering/operational.

Remaining status sequences are winter operational/degraded/degraded/degraded/recovering/operational; cyber operational/strained/degraded/degraded/recovering/recovering; earthquake all operational; wildfire operational/operational/strained/strained/recovering/operational; compound operational/degraded/degraded/critical/critical/critical.

At T+72 compound remains critical at severity 0.5391, pressure 0.6358 and 25,577 affected; coastal remains recovering with zero current hazard, pressure 0.3054 and 8,534 affected. These are deterministic exercise estimates, never observations, forecasts or official classifications.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused gate passes deterministic, bounded, reconciliation, causality and event-attribution contracts for GM0383.
notes: The focused harness passes two tests covering all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services; all values are finite and bounded and intensity-zero semantics are exact.

Every local view reconciles exactly to 36,618 people, no allocated neighbourhood is zero-population, and demand/delivery balances close to floating-point epsilon (maximum observed error approximately 1.42e-14).

Hazard is identical across all eight selected service layers, route flow does not exceed declared logical capacity, and cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic relative to a matched no-event baseline.
These software invariants validate computation, not physical calibration, operator capacity, real customer outage-hours or local outcome accuracy.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The local maps fail both a controlled dune-fire source test and a cross-hazard independence test.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire have exactly the same full nineteen-neighbourhood order: Limmen Oost, Kooiweg, Molendijk, Centrum-Noord, Bakkum-Zuid, Beverwijkerstraatweg, Akersloot West, Akersloot Oost, Noord-End, Buitengebied, Duingebied, Bakkum-Noord, Limmen Centrum, Limmen West, De Woude, Albert's Hoeve, Centrum-Zuid, Duin en Bosch, Oranjebuurt.

With wildfire epicentre set exactly to the Duingebied neighbourhood centre [4.629051192900515, 52.55316001118619], municipality direct-fire intensity is 0.4045, yet Duingebied ranks 11th at 0.4047 while Limmen Oost ranks first at 0.4652 despite its centre being 5.218 km away.

The canonical wildfire source [5.75, 52.18] is 83.108 km from the municipality centre and yields smoke 0.2235 but direct fire zero at T+24; the UI must not imply that this is Castricum's documented dune-fire scenario.

Coastal gives every neighbourhood nonzero hazard from 0.6633 to 0.8934 and ranks Limmen Oost first/Duingebied eleventh without a connected flood footprint; official dune, polder, drainage, heat, fire and cyber evidence cannot support one shared order.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight lifelines reuse six road-derived logical links and generic coefficients rather than Castricum-specific utility, drainage, care or supply dependencies.
notes: Every selected service layer shows the same six A9/N203/N246/N512 route objects and 1,060 abstract nominal units; this is a logical transfer proxy, never physical power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or patient-transfer topology.

At coastal T+24 availability is power 0.4894, water 0.3420, drainage 0.2056, gas 0.6244, telecom 0.2457, mobility 0.2286, facilities 0.4658 and supply 0.3212; no operator or authority source calibrates those exact values.

At compound T+24 availability is power 0.4944, water 0.3357, drainage 0.3065, gas 0.5378, telecom 0.1786, mobility 0.5977, facilities 0.3427 and supply 0.2270; at T+72 all remain identical except facilities decline to 0.2255.

Public provider territories, Liander electricity geometry, partial HHNK objects and RDI sites are valuable typed context. They do not establish safe complete topology, switch/valve/pump/backhaul state, flow, capacity, quality, backup, stock, crews or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: The causal ledger is internally coherent, but its municipality-level amplitudes and intervention/resource assumptions are synthetic rather than locally evidenced.
notes: The model separates direct hazard pressure, recovery, service dependencies/backups and intervention effects and preserves hazard invariance across selected service layers.

This structure correctly allows power loss to cascade into telecom, water, drainage, gas/heating, facilities and supply, consistent with E03/E08, but exact weights and Castricum backup/repair parameters have no operator calibration.

PWN's dune reserve does not prove 0.342 water availability, HHNK pump points do not prove 0.2056 drainage availability, and VRNHN exercise participation does not prove automatic resource arrival or evacuation.

Cyber has no named target, attack path, detection/containment state or authorized operator architecture; affected counts must remain people-equivalent model proxies rather than customers or casualties.

recovery72h.summary: The first-72-hour trajectories are useful stress-test outputs but are not calibrated restoration, evacuation, resource or public-information timelines.
notes: Cumulative event-attributable person-hours at T+72 are storm 453,815.81, pluvial 476,460.88, river 0, coastal 1,430,251.54, heat 326,022.69, winter 601,556.07, cyber 678,069.75, earthquake 27,317.95, wildfire 111,214.59 and compound 1,608,861.61.

At T+72 coastal hazard has ended but all eight services remain below baseline and 8,534 people-equivalent remain affected; compound retains synthetic inundation stress 0.6048 and remains critical with 25,577 affected.

The municipality's three-day preparation advice, PWN reserve statement and VRNHN plans do not specify local household stock, ferry availability, shelter opening, warning/evacuation, mutual aid, fuel, crews, repair order or restoration service levels.

At every checkpoint the interface should keep current hazard, residual service availability, people-equivalent impact, cumulative event-attributable proxy, observed/official/synthetic class, valid time, uncertainty and action status separate.

findings.summary: The coastal preset asserts a severe Castricum inundation and recovery footprint without a selected defence-failure or hydraulic event.
findings.evidence: E05 says the dunes are a managed natural defence and distinguishes future weak-spot analysis from present failure; E07 requires specialist selection and interpretation of LIWO layers. The model nevertheless becomes critical at T+6, holds severity 0.8025 through T+48, reports normalized inundation stress 2.5037 and 25,140 affected at T+24, and retains 8,534 affected at T+72. It has no named sea-level/surge boundary, defence section/state, breach or overtopping, terrain, connected footprint, depth units, arrival, duration, recession, probability class or no-data mask. The exact all-neighbourhood result is therefore unsupported, not validated merely because Castricum is coastal.
findings.action: Block operational interpretation of GM0383 coastal outputs. Require an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/HHNK event with source mechanism, boundary condition, defence state, connected full-resolution footprint, depth/unit, arrival/duration/recession, probability/scenario class, uncertainty, no-data and terms. If no approved event is selected, expose the local footprint/amplitude as Unknown or a clearly labelled minimal hypothetical; never infer a breach or convert unavailable data to zero/safety.

findings.summary: A fire placed at the Duingebied centre ranks that source only eleventh and a neighbourhood 5.218 km away first.
findings.evidence: The controlled T+24 run uses epicentre [4.629051192900515, 52.55316001118619], exactly Duingebied's generated centre, and produces municipality direct-fire 0.4045. Yet Duingebied hazard is 0.4047 at rank 11/19 while Limmen Oost is 0.4652 at rank 1, 5.218 km from the source. E03's June 2026 Castricum exercise says wind, dry vegetation, path structure, vegetation type, current aerial information, firefighting water and possible campsite evacuation govern the real response; its teams also found incompatible maps and communications. The model's inversion is deterministic and cannot be presented as a local fire footprint.
findings.action: Make named ignition/perimeter and source distance spatially controlling, then add authorized RIN/fuel/vegetation, event-valid KNMI wind/moisture, paths/access, firefighting-water and suppression assumptions with explicit uncertainty. Add a regression that a nonzero direct-fire source cell cannot rank behind distant cells without an evidenced propagation mechanism. Keep RIN unavailable/permissioned data Unknown and offer a transparent synthetic fuel surface rather than implied observation.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse the exact same complete neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank nineteen neighbourhoods in precisely the same order from Limmen Oost through Oranjebuurt. E03–E08 instead require different spatial variables: defence-connected hydraulics, polder/sewer catchments, paving/heat/vulnerability, road/ice exposure, fuel/wind/access, utility assets and named cyber targets. The repeated full order, including Limmen Oost first and Duingebied eleventh for both coastal and fire, is a deterministic seed artifact rather than seven calibrated maps.
findings.action: Retire the shared local susceptibility seed. Give each hazard a typed eligibility and source-backed susceptibility surface with provenance, resolution, valid time, completeness, affectsSimulation and explicit Unknown masks. Add cross-hazard independence tests, meaningful eligibility zeros where physically justified, and keep the same scenario hazard invariant when users switch among all eight service layers.

findings.summary: Coastal flooding, pluvial/sewer drainage, surface-water pumping and PWN drinking-water continuity are collapsed into generic scores.
findings.evidence: E05 distinguishes high water-system inundation likelihood in meadows east/northeast, built-up ponding from paving/sewer limits, named polders, retention and 174 partial water-control points. E06 documents a separate Andijk-to-Castricum dune infiltration process, approximately three-week filtration and calamity reserve. The model instead applies the same neighbourhood order to pluvial and coastal hazards and produces exact T+24 water/drainage availability without catchment connectivity, pump directions, unit-safe capacity, sewer surcharge, defence state, pressure, quality/advisory, reserve volume or restoration evidence. No provider polygon for drainage is returned; that is Unknown.
findings.action: Separate North Sea inundation, polder/surface-water, wastewater/sewer surcharge, groundwater/seepage and potable-water pressure/volume/quality states. Integrate licensed HWH/HHNK geometry and expert-selected LIWO context with versioned units and no-data, but keep all 174 points non-causal until connectivity, direction, capacity and state are authorized. Represent PWN's documented process as aggregate dependency/reserve context only; unavailable operational topology remains Unknown or an explicit synthetic zone.

findings.summary: De Woude, coastal access and external acute care require conditional paths that the six-link graph does not represent.
findings.evidence: E02 documents two municipal ferries with daily/seasonal hours, recurring maintenance pauses and outage messaging; the municipality separately approved a cooperation note for emergency services on island De Woude. E03/E04 identify dune paths, limited ordinary beach vehicle access, N513/coastal access and campsite/beach response. The graph contains only six inter-municipal road links, no local N513 logical path, ferry or island dependency. No acute hospital is inside GM0383; the nearest RIVM-listed hospitals are 8.71 and 8.85 km straight-line. Static NWB/GTFS/station/facility records do not establish passability, operation, ambulance time, acceptance, staffing, stock or generator endurance.
findings.action: Add typed internal N513/coastal, Akersloot-ferry and De Woude-ferry access paths with schedule, vehicle class, nominal/Unknown capacity, live-state source and scenario-time closure; do not fabricate a live API where none exists. Couple access loss to mobility, logistics, repair and ambulance travel, not automatic facility closure. Add privacy-safe care-home/primary-care/pharmacy/food/fuel/support-point classes only when officially published and role-verified; external hospital acceptance and occupancy remain Unknown.

findings.summary: One road-derived graph is cloned into eight lifelines without operator-calibrated topology, state, backup or repair.
findings.evidence: Every power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply view reuses the same six road links and 1,060 abstract units. E08 resolves Liander electricity, Stedin gas, PWN water and Ziggo media responsibility at one centre point while drainage returns no record. Public Liander electricity geometry, Stedin downloads, HWH points and RDI sites remain partial/static context; they do not establish complete topology, switching/valves, pressure/flow, backhaul, capacity, quality, backup, stock, damage, crews or restoration. The UI's logical-proxy disclaimer is necessary but does not calibrate exact service availability.
findings.action: Keep NWB causal only for mobility and eligible logistics/repair access. Build separate privacy/security-safe aggregate service zones with uncertainty ranges, or ingest authorized operator aggregates under explicit unit/topology contracts. Every layer/export must expose source, version, valid time, completeness, topologySemantics, observed/context/scenario class and affectsSimulation. Show unavailable or security-sensitive connectivity/state as Unknown, never a cloned road or inferred zero.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour dashboard lacks a validated decision/action ledger and can imply unsupported restoration certainty.
findings.evidence: E04 recommends three-day household preparation and defines municipal reception/communication roles; E03 describes adaptive multi-agency response and explicitly says deployment availability is not guaranteed. Neither supports fixed local preparedness, evacuation, ferry operation, mutual-aid arrival, support points, stock or restoration. Nevertheless the simulation emits exact checkpoint statuses, affected people-equivalent and cumulative person-hours, including coastal recovering with 8,534 affected at T+72 and compound critical with 25,577. No warning, order, request, confirmation, completion, cancellation, responsible owner or evidence time is recorded.
findings.action: Add an action ledger separate from model state with proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled status, owner/authority, timestamp, expiry, source and confidence. At each checkpoint show current hazard, all eight availabilities, people-equivalent affected, cumulative event-attributable proxy and uncertainty together. Label T+72 as the modeled window and preparedness horizon, never a guaranteed recovery deadline.

findings.summary: Storm, heat, winter, cyber, earthquake and canonical wildfire are coherent exercises but lack municipality-specific event calibration.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 support extreme weather, heat/drought, vital-service failure, cyber and coastal wildfire as regional concerns; the risk profile describes regional earthquakes as possible but with very small expected physical effects. No authoritative source validates exact T+24 severities winter 0.6387, cyber 0.4732, heat 0.1163, wildfire 0.1035 or earthquake peak 0.0268. The canonical fire source is 83.108 km away and produces Castricum smoke only, while cyber has no named target/attack path. KNMI data and official event APIs can anchor dated replays, but current observations cannot be relabelled as the canonical scenario or an arbitrary future forecast.
findings.action: Keep these as visibly synthetic stress tests with parameter ranges and sensitivity. For replays pin KNMI/Rijkswaterstaat/RIVM records to event and valid time. Require a named earthquake event plus ground-motion/site/fragility method, a named local fire source/perimeter plus fuel/weather/access, and a named cyber target/attack path before showing direct local precision.

findings.summary: Several zero-result views can be mistaken for zero risk, zero infrastructure or normal operation.
findings.evidence: Examples are river-flood severity/affected/person-hours zero, no drainage provider record, zero RIVM acute hospitals inside the boundary, zero intersecting NDW situation records, and null district-heating/public-charging statistics. These mean respectively a scoped Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screen, incomplete provider mapping, no RIVM-listed acute hospital in-boundary, no records in one snapshot, and unavailable CBS fields. None proves no inland/polder/lake water risk, no drainage responsibility, no accessible care, clear roads or zero infrastructure.
findings.action: Use a three-state contract in maps, legends, tooltips, APIs and exports: measured/modeled zero, Unknown/not covered, and not applicable. Display source, completeness and valid time beside each layer. Add tests that empty provider, hospital and incident intersections and CBS nulls cannot render as safe/operational or zero infrastructure; explain that the river preset excludes Castricum's separate local water mechanisms.

findings.summary: Population allocation is numerically sound but resident-equivalent exposure excludes dynamic coastal, campsite, school, station and care occupancy.
findings.evidence: E01 gives 36,618 municipality residents and rounded neighbourhood rows summing to 36,605; the allocator reconciles exactly. E03/E04 identify coastal recreation, a nearby campsite and vulnerable older residents as context. The model does not include visitors, commuters, beach attendance, campsite guests, school/station occupancy, care-home residents, individual health vulnerability, household supplies or evacuation behaviour. Missing CBS district heat, charging, car and benefit fields remain null as required.
findings.action: Keep resident-equivalent wording, show CBS edition and reconciliation, and never infer people present or individual vulnerability. Add optional privacy-safe daytime/seasonal visitor and facility-occupancy scenarios only with licensed aggregate sources, explicit valid time, provenance and uncertainty.

findings.summary: The focused numerical and semantic invariants pass for GM0383 on the audited build.
findings.evidence: The focused harness passes two tests over all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Outputs are finite and bounded, intensity-zero semantics are exact, 36,618 people reconcile in every local map, demand/delivery balances close to floating-point epsilon, local hazard is service-layer invariant, logical route flow stays within declared capacity, and cumulative person-hours are monotonic and event-attributable against a matched no-event baseline.
findings.action: Retain the focused municipality gate in CI and add regressions for an expert-selected Castricum coastal event, local-fire source ranking, cross-hazard spatial independence, De Woude conditional access and no-data rendering.

corrections.summary: Replace Castricum's generic coastal-distance screen with an expert-selected, defence-aware hydraulic event.
corrections.validation: Before correction coastal is critical from T+6 through T+48, reports severity 0.8025, inundation stress 2.5037 and 25,140 affected at T+24, and retains 8,534 affected at T+72. Require one versioned LIWO/HHNK event with source class, sea boundary, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected full-resolution footprint, depth/unit, arrival/duration/recession, probability/scenario class, uncertainty, no-data and terms. Without approval, local amplitude/footprint must render Unknown or explicitly hypothetical.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared neighbourhood seed and correct source-controlled Castricum dune-fire allocation.
corrections.validation: Before correction seven hazards share the exact complete nineteen-neighbourhood order; a fire at Duingebied's centre ranks it 11th while Limmen Oost 5.218 km away ranks first. Require hazard-specific eligibility and surfaces, a source-cell regression, distinct flood/heat/fire/cyber ordering, explicit Unknown cells, reproducibility and hazard invariance across all selected service layers.

corrections.summary: Separate Castricum coastal, polder/surface-water, sewer, groundwater and drinking-water processes using typed public context.
corrections.validation: Preserve all 174 HWH objects as context until connectivity, direction, capacity units and state are authorized; empty drainage provider mapping remains Unknown. Add separate potable pressure/volume, quality/advisory and wastewater/surface-water states. Version all HHNK/LIWO inputs and test that east/northeast polder susceptibility, built-up sewer ponding and PWN reserve context cannot collapse into one score.

corrections.validation: Add source-backed Akersloot/De Woude ferry and internal coastal/N513 path records with schedule, vehicle class, Unknown live state and scenario-time closure. Test island disconnection and emergency/logistics rerouting without fabricating availability. RIVM/DUO/government points remain dated context and external hospital acceptance, travel, occupancy, staffing and backup remain Unknown without authorized feeds.

corrections.summary: Separate the eight physical/operational lifelines from NWB logical transfer routes.
corrections.validation: NWB must affect mobility and eligible logistics/repair only. Every service layer must declare logical/synthetic/physical topology semantics, source/version/valid time, completeness, unit, uncertainty and affectsSimulation. Provider territories and public register assets cannot imply state. Unavailable/security-sensitive topology, backup, capacity and restoration must render Unknown or as a clearly synthetic aggregate.

corrections.summary: Make source class, no-data, first-72-hour decisions and uncertainty explicit at every operational-looking output.
corrections.validation: Every metric/layer/export must show observed versus official scenario versus synthetic exercise, source/version/valid time, unit, completeness, confidence and affectsSimulation. Render zero, Unknown and not-applicable distinctly. Add proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions with owner and timestamp. At T+72 display residual hazard, all eight availabilities, affected people-equivalent and cumulative event-attributable proxy together; never imply guaranteed restoration.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI/Rijkswaterstaat forecast, official warning, probability estimate, evacuation order, casualty model or operator outage/restoration forecast.

No expert-selected North Sea boundary, current defence state, breach/overtopping, connected LIWO/HHNK footprint, arrival/recession, depth unit, no-data mask or uncertainty is ingested for GM0383; normalized inundation stress is not observed metres.
The river preset's zero is scoped to a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screen and does not establish safety from local polder, canal, Alkmaardermeer, regional-defence, sewer or groundwater mechanisms.

The generalized CBS boundary and deterministic neighbourhood seed do not resolve dunes, polders, catchments, terrain, buildings, paving, shade, fuel, paths, households, beach/campsite visitors or individual vulnerability.
CBS neighbourhood data are rounded/suppressed; the -13 population difference is publication semantics, and null district-heat/charging/car/benefit fields are Unknown rather than zero.

The controlled Duingebied fire inversion and seven-hazard identical rank are deterministic and reproducible; the canonical wildfire is a remote-smoke exercise rather than Castricum's documented dune scenario.
NIPV RIN is a professional one-kilometre product without a verified open bulk interface, licence or cadence; do not screen-scrape or imply it has been ingested.
NWB, GTFS, ProRail and web schedules do not establish incident-time road, rail, bus or ferry operation, capacity, clearance or evacuation throughput; NDW snapshot absence is not an all-clear.

The six-link graph excludes local N513/beach and ferry/island paths and is cloned across eight services; logical connectivity cannot be interpreted as physical utility, telecom, wastewater, patient-transfer or stocked-logistics topology.
HWH's national aggregation is contributor-dependent and partial; 174 points do not define a connected drainage/sewer network or unit-safe usable live capacity.

HHNK direct ArcGIS services expose high-value defence, surface-water, structure and drought-allocation context, but licence, fixed cadence and causal operating-state contracts must be confirmed before redistribution or simulation use.
PWN's public process pages establish Andijk/dune filtration and reserve context but not complete pipe topology, pressure, quality, reserve volume, pump state, backup or restoration.
No complete public causal Liander feeder/switching, Stedin gas pressure/valve, PWN pipe/quality, sewer, Ziggo/mobile backhaul or operator restoration topology is authorized in the model.
Provider territories identify potential responsibility at one reference point, not full-boundary coverage, connectivity, capacity or state; absent drainage mapping remains Unknown.
RDI antenna records do not establish operator, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage, congestion, availability or restoration.
No RIVM acute hospital is inside GM0383 in the dated layer; straight-line distances do not establish travel time, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion or backup endurance.
DUO/government points do not establish command, care, shelter or distribution roles; facilities/supply lack verified care-home, pharmacy, fuel, support-point, stock, depot, vehicle and staff state.
Cyber lacks a named target, attack path, detection/containment evidence and operator architecture; earthquake lacks a selected event, local ground motion/site response and asset fragility.
Generic preparedness, backup, demand, repair and intervention multipliers are exercise controls rather than observed GM0383 resources or commitments.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid changes and 72 hours excludes prolonged flooding, contamination and reconstruction.
